case_name: Debendra Nath Goswami v State of West Bengal
respondent:
State of West Bengal
Supreme Court of India

31 October 1972
W.P. No. 258 of 1972.
The Judgment was delivered by: DUA, J.
1.  Debendra Nath Goswami forwarded through Dum Dum Central Jail an application for a writ in the nature of habeas corpus. That petition purported to be made u/art. 226 of the Constitution and under Section 491, Code of Criminal Procedure. Latter he forwarded another application u/art. 32 of the Constitution from Burdwan Jail where he was apparently transferred in the meantime seeking the same relief.
2.  The petitioner was arrested on December 29, 1971, pursuant to an order of detention made on May 3, 1971. The grounds of detention were served on him at the time of his arrest. The fact of making the detention order was reported to the State Government on May 3, 1971, the day it was made. facts: Debendra Nath Goswami forwarded through Dum Dum Central Jail an application for a writ in the nature of habeas corpus.
The petitioner was arrested on December 29, 1971, pursuant to an order of detention made on May 3, 1971.
His representation was received by the State Government on January 22, 1972, and was considered by it on February 15, 1972.
The delay by the State Government in considering the petitioner's representation is, in our opinion, prima facie unreasonable and it requires satisfactory explanation.
The explanation for this delay is contained in Para 9 of the counter-affidavit sworn by Shri Sukumar Sen, Deputy Secretary, Home (Special) Department, Government of West Bengal on August 21, 1972.
issues: The question of the effect of undue delay on the part of the State Government in considering a detenu's representation has come up before this Court on numerous occasions.

It has consistently been laid down that no hard and fast line can be drawn and that in each case it has to be seen if on the facts and circumstances the State Government can be said to have considered the representation with reasonable dispatch and promptitude realising the importance our Constitution attaches to an individual's right to personal liberty.
respondent_arguments: The explanation for this delay is contained in Para 9 of the counter-affidavit sworn by Shri Sukumar Sen, Deputy Secretary, Home (Special) Department, Government of West Bengal on August 21, 1972.
court_reasoning: It has consistently been laid down that no hard and fast line can be drawn and that in each case it has to be seen if on the facts and circumstances the State Government can be said to have considered the representation with reasonable dispatch and promptitude realising the importance our Constitution attaches to an individual's right to personal liberty.

The explanation for the delay has to satisfy the conscience of the court that the State Government concerned considered the representation with the sense of urgency expected of it by the Constitution.
holding: The petitioner's detention must be held to have become illegal by reason of the unreasonable delay on the part of the State Government in considering his representation.
The petitioner's detention must, therefore, be struck down as illegal and the petitioner directed to be set at liberty.
